title: Completed prefix multiplication kernels and reflection of regular sequences
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $c:R\to S=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R/\mathfrak m^n$ be its canonical completion map [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $f_1,\ldots,f_t\in\mathfrak m$, with $t\geq0$. For $0\leq i<t$, put $P_i=(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$, $M_i=R/P_i$, and $K_i=\ker(f_{i+1}:M_i\to M_i)$. For an $R$-module $N$ write $N^\wedge=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}N/\mathfrak m^nN$. Under the canonical isomorphism $M_i^\wedge\cong S/P_iS$, the completed inclusion $K_i^\wedge\to M_i^\wedge$ identifies $K_i^\wedge$ with $\ker(c(f_{i+1}):S/P_iS\to S/P_iS)$, and the completed multiplication map is multiplication by $c(f_{i+1})$. Moreover $K_i^\wedge=0$ if and only if $K_i=0$. Consequently $f_1,\ldots,f_t$ is an $R$-regular sequence if and only if $c(f_1),\ldots,c(f_t)$ is an $S$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The assertion includes $t=0$.

source.place: Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), part (2), applied to the kernel and image of each prefix multiplication; Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), part (2), and Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK) reflect a zero kernel. The quotient identifications use Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor).

proof.text: Fix $0\leq i<t$ and write $M=M_i$, $f=f_{i+1}$, $K=K_i$, $J=fM$ and $C=M/J$. Both $M$ and $C$ are cyclic, generated by the image of $1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], $K$ and $J$ are finite. The sequences $0\to K\to M\xrightarrow{f}J\to0$ and $0\to J\to M\to C\to0$ are short exact: the first map onto $J$ sends $x$ to $fx$, and the second inclusion is the actual submodule inclusion. These checks use no regularity assumption on the list.

source.place: Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), second assertion; Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), setup for part (2).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor], $M_i^\wedge$ is canonically $S\otimes_R(R/P_i)$. The latter is $S/P_iS$: the maps $s\otimes\bar r\mapsto s c(r)\bmod P_iS$ and $\bar s\mapsto s\otimes\bar1$ are inverse. The first is balanced; the second kills $P_iS$ since $s c(p)\otimes\bar1=s\otimes\bar p=0$ for $p\in P_i$. Their composites are identities on $\bar s$ and on the generating pure tensors, respectively. Under the natural tensor comparison, completed multiplication sends $s\otimes\bar r$ to $s\otimes\overline{fr}$; the displayed quotient map sends this to $s c(f)c(r)$. Hence this is exactly multiplication by $c(f)$ on $S/P_iS$. This also proves the canonical quotient identification without choosing generators or a noncanonical isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (3); explicit balanced-tensor description of its quotient specialization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] to both short exact sequences of step 1. The completed map $M^\wedge\to J^\wedge$ is surjective with kernel the image of the injective $K^\wedge\to M^\wedge$, while $J^\wedge\to M^\wedge$ is injective. Their composite is the completed multiplication map: at every quotient level it is $\bar x\mapsto\overline{fx}$. Since the second factor is injective, the composite has precisely the same kernel as the first factor. Thus the completed inclusion identifies $K^\wedge$ with the multiplication kernel. Step 2 identifies this kernel with the one specified in $S/P_iS$.

source.place: Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), part (2), equivalently Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (2), applied twice.

proof.text: The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated by the Noetherian hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete], part (2), with $I=\mathfrak m$, $M=K$ and $n=1$. If $K^\wedge=0$, its surjection onto $K/\mathfrak mK$ forces this quotient to vanish, hence $K=\mathfrak mK$. The Jacobson radical is $\mathfrak m$, because this is the unique maximal ideal of the local ring. The module $K$ is finite by step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] gives $K=0$. Conversely, if $K=0$, each quotient in its completion is zero, so $K^\wedge=0$. This proves both implications without assuming that completion is faithful on arbitrary modules.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), part (2), at n=1; Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (2).

proof.text: For every $i<t$, steps 2--4 show that multiplication by $f_{i+1}$ on $R/P_i$ is injective if and only if multiplication by $c(f_{i+1})$ on $S/P_iS$ is injective. Put $P_t=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$. As every $f_j\in\mathfrak m$, $P_t\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so $R/P_t\neq0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $\mathfrak mS$ is the maximal ideal of $S$; thus $P_tS\subseteq\mathfrak mS$ and $S/P_tS\neq0$. The prefix injectivity tests together with these nonzero final quotients are precisely [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], proving the claimed equivalence. If $t=0$, there are no prefix tests and $P_t=0$; both nonzero assertions still hold, so both empty sequences are regular.

proof_origin.place: Explicit prefix-kernel assembly from Tags 00MA, 00MB, 05GG and 00DV; final properness from 05GI and regularity from 00LF.

lean.statement: theorem completionPrefixKernelComparison {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (fs : List R) (hfs : ∀ f ∈ fs, f ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) : (∀ i : Fin fs.length, Function.Injective (map (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (prefixMultiplication fs i).ker.subtype) ∧ LinearMap.range ((prefixQuotientEquiv R fs i).toLinearMap.comp (map (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (prefixMultiplication fs i).ker.subtype)) = (completedPrefixMultiplication fs i).ker ∧ (prefixQuotientEquiv R fs i).toLinearMap.comp (map (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (prefixMultiplication fs i)) = (completedPrefixMultiplication fs i).comp (prefixQuotientEquiv R fs i).toLinearMap ∧ (Subsingleton (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (prefixMultiplication fs i).ker) ↔ Subsingleton (prefixMultiplication fs i).ker)) ∧ (RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R fs ↔ RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R) (fs.map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R))))
